name: Tobias Read
subject: An important update from my first month as your Secretary of State
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250127em-nl [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250127em-nl]
Hi folks, it’s Oregon Secretary of State Tobias Read.
As I settle into my new role here in Salem, I wanted to reach out with a quick update on what’s been happening in your state government over the past few weeks:
→ Mari Watanabe was sworn in following her appointment as the new State Representative for House District 34 following Lisa Reynolds’s move to the state Senate. As Oregon’s first Japanese-American legislator, Representative Watanabe has made history — and I was thrilled to have the honor of presiding over her swearing-in.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250127em-nl [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250127em-nl]
→ Dena Dawson began her role as Elections Director on Tuesday. With over 15 years of election administration experience, she will help this office safeguard Oregon’s democracy and ensure our elections run smoothly. With experience in Colorado, Nevada, and Oregon, I’m confident she has what it takes to help deliver for the people over the next four years.
With so much change coming from Washington over the past few weeks, I want Oregonians to rest assured that the Secretary of State’s office is working around the clock to defend our democracy and protect our communities.
With Mari, Dena, and so many others serving our state, I’ve never been more optimistic about its future and its capacity to deliver for the people.
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?refcode=250127em-nl]
Thanks for all you do,
Tobias Read
P.S. Don’t forget! The Oregon Political Tax Credit allows you to donate $50 (if you file single) or $100 (if you file joint) to a candidate, PAC, or party, which will be fully credited back as a rebate — so it’s free to donate! | | **For Immediate Release:** January 27, 2025

**Contact:** Gage Hoekstra, Press Secretary, **[ghoekstra@indiana.gop](mailto:greid@indiana.gop "greid@indiana.gop")**

**Indiana GOP Applauds Braun’s Commitment To School Choice** **INDIANAPOLIS (January 27, 2025)** – The Indiana Republican Party released the following statement regarding the School Choice Week on January 27, 2025.**
****
**"With National School Choice Week upon us, the Indiana Republican Party commends Governor Mike Braun on his proposal to expand school choice to all students, giving every family the opportunity to pursue the best education for their child.

Governor Braun is also working to support our teachers through increased pay, ensuring Indiana can recruit and retain qualified and committed educators. It’s Sally Field. I’m proud to call Jane Fonda a dear friend, and I fully believe in the necessary work of her climate PAC. This month has been devastating for our hometown of Los Angeles. Fires ripped through my neighborhood, destroying homes, memories, and dreams. Thanks to the heroic efforts of my neighbors and first responders, my house miraculously survived — but many others weren't so lucky. My heart aches for them. What’s happening right now in Southern California is a powerful snapshot of our climate nightmare. Climate disasters are happening everywhere — wildfires, floods, hurricanes — all fueled by the fossil fuel industry’s greed and a government that won’t hold them accountable. And now, with Trump’s administration gleefully rolling back climate protections and empowering polluters at every turn, there’s no time to waste. While we fight Trump’s deadly agenda, _we need to be strategic._ We do that by investing in candidates at the state and local level and building a robust layer of climate policy to protect our neighbors and our communities from this administration’s deadly agenda. In 2024, Jane’s team helped elect nearly 100 leaders at every level of government across the country. Now, they’re hitting the ground running to identify as many climate champions as possible to support this year and beyond. But they need you on their team. **That’s why I’m asking for your help today. If you can, please join me in supporting their crucial work with a contribution of any amount.** I’ve not only had the great pleasure to work with Jane on-screen as an actor, but I’ve also been right there on the front lines with Jane as an activist — marching, protesting, and yes, even getting arrested together when we refused to stay silent about the climate crisis. This fight is deeply personal, and the stakes couldn’t be higher. **[Whether it’s $10, $25, or $100, your donation will make a powerful difference. clean_body: | = Hi there. It’s Sally Field. I’m proud to call Jane Fonda a dear friend, and I fully believe in the necessary work of her climate PAC. This month has been devastating for our hometown of Los Angeles. Fires ripped through my neighborhood, destroying homes, memories, and dreams. Thanks to the heroic efforts of my neighbors and first responders, my house miraculously survived — but many others weren't so lucky. My heart aches for them. What’s happening right now in Southern California is a powerful snapshot of our climate nightmare. Climate disasters are happening everywhere — wildfires, floods, hurricanes — all fueled by the fossil fuel industry’s greed and a government that won’t hold them accountable. And now, with Trump’s administration gleefully rolling back climate protections and empowering polluters at every turn, there’s no time to waste. While we fight Trump’s deadly agenda, we need to be strategic. We do that by investing in candidates at the state and local level and building a robust layer of climate policy to protect our neighbors and our communities from this administration’s deadly agenda. In 2024, Jane’s team helped elect nearly 100 leaders at every level of government across the country. Now, they’re hitting the ground running to identify as many climate champions as possible to support this year and beyond. But they need you on their team. That’s why I’m asking for your help today. If you can, please join me in supporting their crucial work with a contribution of any amount. I’ve not only had the great pleasure to work with Jane on-screen as an actor, but I’ve also been right there on the front lines with Jane as an activist — marching, protesting, and yes, even getting arrested together when we refused to stay silent about the climate crisis. This fight is deeply personal, and the stakes couldn’t be higher. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = With love and gratitude, Sally Field P.S. — I know not everyone is in a position to afford making a financial contribution to emails like this one. Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for re-election so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in the United States Senate. The Radical Left has him circled as a prime target to defeat in the 2026 Midterm Elections. Can he count on your support? _

Tommy Tuberville | Meet Coach Tuberville: Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces. In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud. In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson. In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville's time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year's Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP's SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul "Bear" Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others. In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime. Now, Coach Tuberville is running for re-election so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in the United States Senate. AP: Trump’s new Justice Department leadership orders a freeze on civil rights cases [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=012725_2&amount=25]
Even if we knew this was coming, Team, it's still bad: The Justice Department has ordered the civil rights division to halt much of its investigative activity and not pursue new indictments, cases or settlements , according to a memo sent to the temporary head of the division.
The letter instructs the division to ensure that civil rights attorneys do not file “ any new complaints, motions to intervene, agreed-upon remands, amicus briefs, or statements of interest. ” Another memo directed attorneys to notify leadership of any settlements or consent decrees — court-enforceable agreements to reform police agencies — that were finalized by the Biden administration within the last 90 days.
It's worth noting that these memos pertain to the work done by nonpartisan civil servants, lawyers who are career DOJ employees and serve regardless of who is president. Any presidential appointees from the last administration ended their jobs when Trump was inaugurated.

| Dear Hello I've tried to only send you the highlights each day, "cutting to the Chase", if you will.
However, as we get closer to crossover, next Tuesday, the number of bills and the implications of the bills to be discussed and debated are great. So please pay close attention. There are many bills that need your attention.
Please click on each of the links above and carefully read the descriptions. We have much work to do and only a short period of time to accomplish our grassroots efforts.
Tomorrow morning at 7:30am in the Senate Subcommittee on Resources, is the huge battle over both President Trump and Governor Youngkin's initiative, "No tax on tips."
Elimination of the car tax for low income individuals will also come up tomorrow.
There's a bill that would give caregivers, who are family members a tax credit.
Ranked choice voting is on the docket in the Senate Finance and Appropriations Committee. We must oppose any method of nomination that confuses voters.
There are also gun bills like SB1450, which creates standards of "responsible conduct" for firearm industry members and requires such members to establish and implement reasonable controls regarding the manufacture, sale, distribution, use and marketing of the firearm industry.
Homeschooling families who homeschool under the religious exemption should call in this Tuesday to push back against SB1031 Pekarsky.
There are plenty of corporate welfare bills that should be opposed, along with bills expanding the size of government using authorities, which are unelected and unaccountable to you. I cringe every time I see our elected officials introduce bills that grow the size of government.
This is state corporatism.
I really hate calling out Republicans. I really do. But sadly, many seem to have lost their way. There are some Republicans who need to be respectfully, and kindly reminded of our Republican Creed. It's time for some accountability.
We are counting on Republicans to support limited government and reduce or eliminate taxes.
Does your bill grow the size of government?
Then don't introduce it. Please tell the lobbyist or person asking you to introduce the bill, "NO."
Unfortunately, Republicans are introducing bills to expand spending on non-core functions of government.
---
| |
---
Many times I've asked, why are we are balancing our budget on alcohol, gambling and marijuana?
Look no further than [VPAP](https://byh4wqwab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Exq-4rsrAYsCmIKbNiLvBBWguMuTd5W1xQ-WPMhRUWlwwlHp7snWPGd6FR-6a6kTk0xaaqSVqYrK4zyfadSp_fg6MSObwILb9M1nqaxXpXCsk7j2GocEJmgy__YqfPb0SikxYv3LqZ-KrIylwhEN2Q==&c=voUNKiXwXdjLg3yhreDkPiswo35nKC_rUmJ8tvlF5_mwscwRGJHD_w==&ch=jKGovgB2miqbu0QfULJola1Oqhu5wMF5Pt04MIQZyujs5J9hOPOf2A==) or the Virginia Public Access Project to see who is funding each legislator.
Friends, I've given you the tools you need to hold your elected officials accountable.
What you do with it is up to you. Let's work together to make Virginia Great Again.

body:
| Hi Peter,

I know the first weeks of the New Year have probably hit hard. It’s more than frustrating to watch a convicted felon take our nation's highest office. For me, it brought back memories of January 2017, and the anger, sadness, shock, and horror of seeing our progress put on the chopping block.

And now, here we are again. The thing is, we fought back then, and if you’re feeling that same weight, Peter, _I want to ask you to channel that frustration into action._ Trump isn’t going to waste a single moment putting his extremist agenda into motion, and he’s already rescinded Biden’s 2022 order, "Lowering Prescription Drug Costs for Americans" which will likely have devastating consequences for millions of Americans who rely on affordable medications. Trump is already paving the way for Big Pharma to continue hiking prices unchecked, leaving families, seniors, and those with chronic illnesses to bear the financial burden.

[**Peter, this is the first end-of-month deadline of 2025, and we can’t afford to sit on the sidelines while Trump puts profits over people. Every dollar raised helps build the infrastructure we need to, protect everyday Americans, and fight for progress at every level. body:
https://www.lateefahsimon.com [https://www.lateefahsimon.com]
Friend,
The past couple of weeks have been a whirlwind for Congresswoman Lateefah Simon – and we’re thrilled to share some of the incredible milestones and moments from her historic start in Congress.
Since the day she was sworn in, Lateefah vowed to fight every day for CA-12 and the values we hold dear. Since then, she has:
* Delivered her first speech on the House floor , opposing HR 30 – a harmful bill that hurts survivors and immigrants without improving public safety.
* Cast her first votes as a member of Congress , bringing our East Bay values to Washington.
* Secured over $5 million in federal funding for critical investments for our community’s future, including reconnecting Oakland's Chinatown to the waterfront.
* Joined key committees and caucuses, including the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability, the Reproductive Freedom Caucus, and the House Committee on Small Business.
* Been appointed as the first-ever National Finance Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus PAC.
But, Friend, as much as Lateefah has been busy, spending every single day championing the East Bay’s needs and fighting for our rights, President Donald Trump has also been busy...
Trump and his allies have wasted no time advancing their dangerous agenda . In just his first week, House Republicans have already started pushing extremist policies that target our communities, dismantle progress, and threaten our democracy.
We need to meet this moment with strength and determination. As Lateefah takes on the fight in Congress, we need your support to ensure she can keep pushing back against the GOP’s harmful agenda and delivering for the East Bay.
With our first end-of-month deadline of the year in just ONE WEEK, can we count on you to stand with Lateefah by chipping in $10, $25, or whatever you can today? Every dollar helps sustain this movement and fight back against Trump’s extremism. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lateefah-for-congress-uplift?refcode=X_012725_janrecap]

subject: Going Back to Our Roots
body:
| | | | | | [](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2w89iu-uftkso-kyd76rh7/)
---
**Going Back to Our Roots**
---
Hello friend, I think I can speak for all of us when I say that we, as a progressive community, have been going through a lot lately. Since Election Day—and maybe even a little before that—we’ve been stuck in a constant cycle of anxiety, angst, anger, sadness, resilience, and even hopelessness. Sometimes, we cycle through all these emotions in a single day. The country we know and love is deteriorating before our very eyes. The policies being enacted are both cruel and bewildering. The rhetoric coming from the White House, the mainstream media, and certain members of Congress has crossed every imaginable line of decency and sensibility. I could go on and on about how bad things have gotten, but I know I’m preaching to the choir. The reason I’m writing and sharing this is that I’ve been holding in these thoughts all weekend, and my form of therapy is connecting with my community. I am so grateful for the No Dem Left Behind community and the larger progressive movement. In times like these, we must lean on one another. Early in the days of No Dem Left Behind, we had a saying: _We will never bring up a problem without also sharing solutions or ideas to address it._ **I’m going back to our roots here.** As progressive visionary Teddy Roosevelt once said:___"There are many qualities which we need in order to gain success, but the three above all—for the lack of which no brilliancy and no genius can atone—are Courage, Honesty and Common Sense.”_ You’ll see report after report about the 2024 elections—why we lost, what went wrong, who stayed home, etc. No Dem Left Behind will be releasing our own comprehensive report soon, so keep an eye out for that. Reports are essential for understanding our mistakes and learning how to grow. But this moment requires more than reflection—it requires action. What we’re working on this cycle is getting back to basics: identifying community leaders who are already trusted and respected where they live because of the work they do, and recruiting those people to run for Congress. The House of Representatives should truly represent America. We are not all lawyers, former prosecutors, or millionaires. Our country is made up of incredible working people—teachers, firefighters, small business owners, and so many others. Sadly, our current Congress doesn’t reflect that reality, and as a result, we see policies that hurt our communities rather than help them. Leadership is what we need above all else. Democratic allies in Congress face a daunting challenge over the next two years, but we are counting on them to rise to the occasion. And if they don’t, we are prepared to hold them accountable. We’ve seen how Trump uses the primary lever to intimidate those who step out of line, and we can’t be afraid to use it ourselves. This doesn’t mean we’ll primary someone over minor disagreements. But we will challenge those who vote with Republicans or parrot their talking points. Joe Manchin and Kyrsten Sinema betrayed us time and again, and now it seems **_John Fetterman is following in their footsteps._** His hesitation on the recent January 6 vote to condemn the pardons of those who stormed the Capitol was utterly unacceptable. And then there’s the courts. Donald Trump controls a radical, right-wing Supreme Court, and the corruption we see there is undeniable. Across the country, Americans from all political backgrounds are growing increasingly skeptical of SCOTUS. It is corrupt and compromised, and we must shine a light on this to force Congress and the public to address it. Americans—whether Republican, Democrat, or Independent—can get behind a simple, powerful message: _We want an unbiased, corruption-free Supreme Court._ The road ahead is long, but we cannot afford to sit back. This moment requires bold action, fearless leadership, and a united progressive movement ready to stand up for what’s right. [**_Here’s what I’m asking of you: Will you join us in this fight? Donate today to help us recruit strong, community-based leaders for Congress and continue holding our elected officials accountable. Every dollar helps us organize, fight, and make progress for the America we all believe in. Together, we can turn frustration into action. Together, we can win._**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2w89iu-uftksp-kyd76rh8/)

Derek — In
just two days, as a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, I will vote
on the nomination of Pam Bondi. Here are some thoughts...

Earlier this month, I had the opportunity to ask Attorney General nominee
Pam Bondi some questions.

Her answers were not just disappointing — they were downright
disqualifying for someone who wants to be the top law enforcement officer
in the country.

When asked whether she could acknowledge that President Trump lost in
2020, she apparently could not.

When asked whether she would preserve the evidence gathered by the Justice
Department in the January 6 insurrection investigation, she would not
commit to doing so.

When asked whether she would come after Trump’s opponents with the powers
of the Justice Department — something he has repeatedly threatened to do —
her answer was evasive and unconvincing.

Derek, Pam Bondi
has not demonstrated that she will be an Attorney General for the American
people, placing her loyalty to the Constitution and her oath of office
over her fidelity to Donald Trump. That’s not just a conflict of interest
— that’s a danger to our democracy because it means that she will be less
focused on attacking crime and potentially more focused on attacking
Trump’s perceived enemies.

Birthright citizenship guarantees that children born in the United States are citizens, regardless of the immigration status of their parents.** His action violated the Constitution and has already been blocked by a Reagan-era federal judge. This is just one piece of his cruel and inhumane scheme to target vulnerable immigrant communities across the country. I am glad Oregon is one of the many states suing to block President Trump's executive order ending birthright citizenship. Our nation is largely made up of immigrants and the descendants of immigrants, and we need to support our neighbors who are afraid of their families being ripped apart. **Make no mistake: No president, including Trump, can overturn the Constitution with an executive order.****_But it won't stop him and his MAGA cronies from trying to do everything they can to decimate our constitutional rights._** The 14th Amendment is clear – birthright citizenship is the law of the land. Birthright citizenship guarantees that children born in the United States are citizens, regardless of the immigration status of their parents. His action violated the Constitution and has already been blocked by a Reagan-era federal judge. This is just one piece of his cruel and inhumane scheme to target vulnerable immigrant communities across the country. I am glad Oregon is one of the many states suing to block President Trump's executive order ending birthright citizenship. Our nation is largely made up of immigrants and the descendants of immigrants, and we need to support our neighbors who are afraid of their families being ripped apart. Make no mistake: No president, including Trump, can overturn the Constitution with an executive order.But it won't stop him and his MAGA cronies from trying to do everything they can to decimate our constitutional rights. The 14th Amendment is clear – birthright citizenship is the law of the land. body:
Some thoughts on playing the long game:
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20250127-1&t=1&akid=1673%2E587540%2EI9uVIa)
Peter, one of the key aspects that sets Leaders We Deserve apart is that we’re playing the long game. I’ve said this over and over because it’s super important:
**Democrats need to build our bench with young progressive leaders TODAY so they can lead our country tomorrow.** A young candidate we’re electing to a state legislature right now could very well be the future President of the United States.
**[We elected six young leaders to state legislatures and Congress in 2024 – and Peter, we’re just getting started. Pitch in $5 and help keep up the fight.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20250127-1?refcode=em20250127-1673&amount=5&refcode2=1673_587540_I9uVIa&akid=1673%2E587540%2EI9uVIa)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20250127-1?amount=5&refcode=em20250127-1673&refcode2=1673_587540_I9uVIa&akid=1673%2E587540%2EI9uVIa)**
In college, I studied the way conservative political movements built their power over the past 30 years, winning control of state legislatures and appointing a ton of far-right judges to advance their agenda. It didn’t happen out of nowhere – conservatives and Republicans worked tirelessly to get to where they are now.
It was a major wake-up call for me – and one of the reasons I helped start Leaders We Deserve. We have a generation of young people who are ready to step up and lead. These are the progressive leaders who will write the future of this country, who will fight for our values and create the progress that we need to see. But they need our support today to win their elections and start building those movements.
I know the results of the presidential election were extremely disappointing. Like you, I’m worried about what the future holds under a second Trump administration.
But the work we’re doing at Leaders We Deserve was always much bigger than the presidential election. I take comfort in the fact that we elected six new young people across the country – and that we’ll continue to grow that number year after year, cycle after cycle. We are building a solid foundation for a progressive future.
**[Peter, can we count on you to play the long game with us? Donate $5 now to power our work electing the next generation of progressive leaders.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20250127-1?refcode=em20250127-1673&amount=5&refcode2=1673_587540_I9uVIa&akid=1673%2E587540%2EI9uVIa)**
Thank you!!
David Hogg

name: Kristen McDonald Rivet
subject: [photo enclosed] Today’s swearing-in ceremony!
body:
|
#
Friend, Earlier today, with family and community members by my side, I had the honor of participating in a district swearing-in ceremony in Flint. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/101077512/524842130/-1606559029?refcode=em-1.27.25-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0MWM4M2FiMy0wNmRkLWVmMTEtODhmOC0wMDIyNDgyYTk1NzkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=8cxYxGCANgoK-AbPYnLJIRKtsMuz6EPn9tyImPjrj4o=) While I _officially_ was sworn into office in Washington earlier this month, today was a special opportunity to celebrate this moment with the folks who powered this campaign – the members of this coalition. We won in November because neighbors of all political stripes united behind our vision of practical, commonsense leadership focused on delivering real results for our community – a real, forward focusing coalition rather than tired talking points and cynical rhetoric. **For years now, you’ve heard me say that our movement is about “we not me,” and today's ceremony wasn't just about me taking an oath. * **TOP NEWS**

“**Multi-agency operation targeted immigrants in Austin and San Antonio,** ” Texas Tribune's **Pooja Salhotra** — “Agents from multiple federal agencies carried out immigration enforcement operations in Austin and San Antonio on Sunday, federal officials said.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, along with the Drug Enforcement Agency, the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives collaborated on “enhanced targeted operations” in both cities, an ICE spokesperson said. A similar operation took place Sunday morning in the Rio Grande Valley, [a local station reported](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eIdQy0_MopUrebdmXRPTEI0m4VNLfTlNHIoxbYALVEbPWI58FBqXDy81iOdjwQFOOKA9tKAYu3ZaaEBBdsGXtdA7HKsYDOnsgsAkNeTo4uA04T2_UQTJW6YfAZ7DUBVklgE0yzuFp7V6vWmfkgCD48H4w53MHICu3PSKARA4mHQ66rFTZ22Y_QCKlcvgADobhNWYXX2U4bFHbA_0FHSaXYLzwb8TpVO0kEwrp5P7mhpNjLshNOHyC56gBv8zSItoHY5RNJUUOvT8icN-G5jJmp0w6CPW6TI5Fy6_kMlLUa-VIBK4PE9I7ryCdvCvAEm9BcA_XHYqIALYlqHUBF3XyAJrxwep9xabYYgzEFelsGmBa8F4p-7kzGNs3Bcv0ZZp2kB4ShGl7hgNHGpWCP_Cjh8/4di/zsAYY95ITXivb1prDHdWsg/h9/h001.3zjNII_PRH7JW4EyQUA2m_5bmSmk8DMUxBighwliL-A).

The spokesperson said the operations were to “enforce U.S. immigration law and preserve public safety and national security by keeping potentially dangerous criminal aliens out of our communities.” The official did not say what kind of offenses the targeted individuals were suspected of committing or whether anyone was detained.

KXAN [first reported](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.xjnMFfva-73dHOne5Rc0eBfPaR82fkoe3IjF2o__4VYaxDIgRmr3j1ie-6e0C7kMieHVTkUF2YAWUKLRyqqsTnX9VbPavrmspTVOQ_ip14WFsuBJ_-4m4iCWJTVrOirYNz1N8AwaysUY2VFh4mb-cXuvo3-lqkEJ8xWU7aKUWWiH-sfbdOf9oslYbOIYey23n2c75uCqxwjXO-0kp33iXJshVt-fmm6hVzWEXZ-HVzR5xAYBzBwvAqEr6S6_sZIvOtQfx_gvELoO04rzAwutI4PzbkEcLdNeg5JbWrAs6gP6eSkrSgy8ZMKMturHEPTNLAo9F0k_D2_PWjyDw3PNFeOOF1ZUORfKoryZh5oDsiA4t_1M63bHlyHJYMW7xs8LbTRo9b9z-VSDXave20DnwA/4di/zsAYY95ITXivb1prDHdWsg/h10/h001.WReP4w3PbLcuKyVazko-befNpHeas3vC1xuuthkamfU) ICE was conducting an operation in the Austin area on Sunday afternoon through a spokesperson for the DEA’s Houston division. DEA spokesperson **Sally Sparks** said the agency’s Houston office “mobilized every agent in our division,” whose jurisdiction spans from Brownsville to Corpus Christi, Del Rio and Waco.

“We got information that we had to mobilize, so we mobilized,” Sparks told The Texas Tribune. “The majority of our agents assisted.”

A Houston DEA [post on X](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/ss/c/u001.Tb7ejk-5QfVnOrZFvpt2rihooPa139LbrleqEejZSjLF_Js2L0HNFrBDLpqEgdyJSoAqI3RTcZIYYasCfTRaciPIdr08y8fyQ1eGLmFQhmgLqmJhxNQZS41c59f5A7IupoaurD5sdzspPF0fNMiuKBUjU8Cdi8fcuYMJ4upSxY4M6ZdD8vIqOCpT86h_wZXynJj9sahEmH9KOp0-o0j0A5fYnAqjmQR3FtlmPE-xaodJf6t6tDb-crw-0NTpXxkL7wJt-XuCkQlOjfmbYaJ8N7AcM6-t5lGYRAgLVZXu60H2j99h6gYdijufJv3uXv1gcoWHc-SBjiEJdFgwbj0I21wx7J59oeIay19kRL2N7zbOOZsas8kjz6qst7xmxp90/4di/zsAYY95ITXivb1prDHdWsg/h12/h001.5J3NI6Rpfy6R1Sx-i7wvF6MxQtjPdY-Wbx9xNQDlRzo) on Sunday showed photos of law enforcement officers in a residential area escorting a man in handcuffs.

Neither ICE nor the DEA answered questions about the scale of the operations. Spokespeople for the Travis and Bexar counties’ sheriff’s offices said they had not been notified of the operations. “**Texas job growth outpaces national average in 2024, adding 284k,** ” San Antonio Express-News' **Sara DiNatale** — “Texas employers grew the state’s job count by 2% last year — outpacing the national average — adding a total of 284,200 jobs.

The latest figures from the Texas Workforce Commission show the growth continued in December, when another 37,500 jobs were added. That helped push the state’s full-year growth rate 0.6 percentage points higher than the national average.

Texas finished the year with a record 14.32 million positions.

“This new record-high level for jobs and the civilian labor force shows the strength of Texas’ economy,” Texas Workforce Chairman **Bryan Daniel** said in a statement.

The labor force, a tally that includes both those working and actively looking for work, hit nearly 15.6 million in December. That was up about 3.5% from a year earlier.

Texas’ seasonally adjusted unemployment held steady at 4.2%, just above the national average of 4.1%.

The leading sector for job growth in December was professional and business services, adding 17,800 jobs. The trade, transportation, and utilities sector added 10,400 jobs while the hospitality sector added 3,700.

The San Antonio-New Braunfels metro area’s unadjusted unemployment rate dropped to 3.4% from 3.9% in November. It was 3.1% a year ago. The area added 2,400 jobs over the month.

While hospitality helped lead statewide growth, the San Antonio area lost 1,000 of the service-oriented jobs in December. The trade and utilities sector accounted for the biggest boost locally with 2,400 new positions. Private education and health services, a combined sector, added 900 jobs.

“The Texas economy is thriving in diverse sectors,” said Commissioner **Alberto Treviño III**.

Unemployment fell to 3.1% in the Austin-Round Rock metro area from 3.5% in November. It was up from 3% a year ago.

The state’s lowest unemployment rate of 2.4% was recorded in the Midland metro area. It was followed by Amarillo at 2.6% and the College Station-Bryan area at 2.7%.

The McAllen-Edinburg-Mission metro reported the highest unemployment rate at 6.2%. It was followed by Beaumont-Port Arthur at 5.6% and Brownsville-Harlingen at 5.1%." “He was trailblazing,” his son said Sunday. “He was really upsetting the establishment, and they let him have it.”

“The man was also a feat,” Patrick Bernal said of his father’s longevity. “He was in perfect health. His vitals were just amazing. He wasn't ill. He didn't take medication. He just went to sleep.”

“**Texas lawmakers race against fundraising moratorium to fill campaign coffers,** ” Dallas Morning News'**Karen Brooks Harper** and**Nolan D. McCaskill** — “Few things focus the mind of a politician, and political donors, more than a fundraising deadline.

For three decades, a blackout period around the Legislature’s regular session has barred Texas lawmakers from raising political money while they tackle the state’s business in the Capitol.

The Texas Legislature meets every two years for 140 days. What lawmakers choose as priorities, and how they conduct their business, will affect the lives of Texans for years.

Dec. 14 was the last day to raise campaign cash for the session that began last week, and the state’s 181 lawmakers responded to the deadline with gusto, raising a combined $13 million in two weeks — a number that jumps closer to $17 million when fundraising by Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, who presides over the Senate, is added.

The dash for cash in the two weeks preceding the session moratorium awes even the most veteran of political insiders — particularly as the skyrocketing cost of running a campaign requires officials to raise ever higher piles of money.

“Hell, it’s crazy,” longtime lobbyist **Bill Miller,** of Austin-based Hillco Partners, said of the biennial presession fundraising sprints. “There are multiple fundraisers every day, and they’re all over the place. There are so many fundraisers you can’t even count them.”

One of the most visible examples was the parade of lawmakers and lobbyists into the Austin Club, an exclusive gathering spot near the Capitol where political fundraisers stacked up in one- and two-hour time slots — nearly 60 private events in the first two weeks of December.

At the events, lawmakers wait in a designated room while lobbyists and other invited donors swing by with checks — sometimes getting a minute or two with the lawmaker, sometimes just dropping a check on a table at the door before moving on to the next one, according to several lawmakers and lobbyists who attended the events.

The fundraising frenzy at the private club between Election Day and the session blackout period was just the tip of the iceberg.

In-person and online fundraisers across the state had checks pouring into campaign coffers right up to midnight on the last day before the blackout." Become a PAID subscriber for $5/mo or $50/yr . | TOP NEWS “Multi-agency operation targeted immigrants in Austin and San Antonio, ” Texas Tribune's Pooja Salhotra — “Agents from multiple federal agencies carried out immigration enforcement operations in Austin and San Antonio on Sunday, federal officials said. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, along with the Drug Enforcement Agency, the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives collaborated on “enhanced targeted operations” in both cities, an ICE spokesperson said. A similar operation took place Sunday morning in the Rio Grande Valley, . The spokesperson said the operations were to “enforce U.S. immigration law and preserve public safety and national security by keeping potentially dangerous criminal aliens out of our communities.” The official did not say what kind of offenses the targeted individuals were suspected of committing or whether anyone was detained. KXAN ICE was conducting an operation in the Austin area on Sunday afternoon through a spokesperson for the DEA’s Houston division. DEA spokesperson Sally Sparks said the agency’s Houston office “mobilized every agent in our division,” whose jurisdiction spans from Brownsville to Corpus Christi, Del Rio and Waco. | “We got information that we had to mobilize, so we mobilized,” Sparks told The Texas Tribune. “The majority of our agents assisted.” A Houston DEA on Sunday showed photos of law enforcement officers in a residential area escorting a man in handcuffs. Neither ICE nor the DEA answered questions about the scale of the operations. Spokespeople for the Travis and Bexar counties’ sheriff’s offices said they had not been notified of the operations. A spokesperson for U.S. Rep. Lloyd Doggett , D-Austin, said Doggett did not receive advance notice that ICE would conduct an operation in Austin. Sunday’s operations came less than one week after President Donald Trump began his second term as president and promised mass deportations across the country. Trump issued more than a dozen immigration-related executive orders last week, including that lets migrants make appointments to request asylum and authorizing immigration officers to raid sensitive locations such as churches, schools and hospitals." “Texas job growth outpaces national average in 2024, adding 284k, ” San Antonio Express-News' Sara DiNatale — “Texas employers grew the state’s job count by 2% last year — outpacing the national average — adding a total of 284,200 jobs. The latest figures from the Texas Workforce Commission show the growth continued in December, when another 37,500 jobs were added. That helped push the state’s full-year growth rate 0.6 percentage points higher than the national average. Texas finished the year with a record 14.32 million positions. “This new record-high level for jobs and the civilian labor force shows the strength of Texas’ economy,” Texas Workforce Chairman Bryan Daniel said in a statement. The labor force, a tally that includes both those working and actively looking for work, hit nearly 15.6 million in December. That was up about 3.5% from a year earlier. Texas’ seasonally adjusted unemployment held steady at 4.2%, just above the national average of 4.1%. The leading sector for job growth in December was professional and business services, adding 17,800 jobs. The trade, transportation, and utilities sector added 10,400 jobs while the hospitality sector added 3,700. The San Antonio-New Braunfels metro area’s unadjusted unemployment rate dropped to 3.4% from 3.9% in November. It was 3.1% a year ago. The area added 2,400 jobs over the month. While hospitality helped lead statewide growth, the San Antonio area lost 1,000 of the service-oriented jobs in December. The trade and utilities sector accounted for the biggest boost locally with 2,400 new positions. Private education and health services, a combined sector, added 900 jobs. “The Texas economy is thriving in diverse sectors,” said Commissioner Alberto Treviño III. Unemployment fell to 3.1% in the Austin-Round Rock metro area from 3.5% in November. It was up from 3% a year ago. The state’s lowest unemployment rate of 2.4% was recorded in the Midland metro area. It was followed by Amarillo at 2.6% and the College Station-Bryan area at 2.7%. The McAllen-Edinburg-Mission metro reported the highest unemployment rate at 6.2%. It was followed by Beaumont-Port Arthur at 5.6% and Brownsville-Harlingen at 5.1%." ($) “Legendary legislator and educator from San Antonio dies, ” San Antonio Express-News' Elaine Ayala — “Joe J. Bernal , a in San Antonio best known for championing the state’s earliest bilingual education laws, died Saturday at 97. He was at home in San Antonio, surrounded by his family, and wearing his Bernal Middle School “Black Knights” shirt, relatives said. Bernal's family was already in mourning as his death came just one day after his granddaughter Bianca Ambriz died of cancer. Bernal’s wife Mary Esther Bernal , one of the city’s earliest bilingual education teachers and equally as popular as her husband, died in 2022. “They were quite a team to get through those tough times in the old days of civil rights,” their son Patrick Bernal said Sunday. In 2006, Bernal spoke to the Voces Oral Project at the University of Texas at Austin about the rampant discrimination Mexican Americans faced. “In the service, we were American soldiers,” the World War II veteran said. “But back home, we were Mexicans,” a term that stood out as a slur in the mouths of those who used it for people of Mexican descent whether they were U.S. citizens or not. “He was trailblazing,” his son said Sunday. “He was really upsetting the establishment, and they let him have it.” “The man was also a feat,” Patrick Bernal said of his father’s longevity. “He was in perfect health. His vitals were just amazing. He wasn't ill. He didn't take medication. He just went to sleep.” Bernal was admired for both his military and legislative service. “Whenever we went out in public, I can't tell you the number of people that would come up to him, because they looked at him as a hero,” standing to greet everyone, he said. “He was proud to be from the West Side of San Antonio, and that was what drove him – to better the lives of the people that he knew from his neighborhood.” In his legislative career, Bernal first focused on various preschool through grade 12 initiatives, later widening his scope to higher education. He became a leading advocate for the creation of the University of Texas at San Antonio." ($) | #TXLEGE “Texas Gov Greg Abbott to unveil his legislative priorities, ” Houston Chronicle'sBenjamin Wermund — “Gov. Greg Abbott is set to lay out his priorities — almost certain to — in his State of the State address this weekend. The Texas Republican’s address will air on TV at 5 p.m. Sunday. Abbott is again bucking the longstanding tradition of addressing state lawmakers during a joint session at the Capitol, instead delivering his address to cameras from an oil company in Austin. The address comes after Abbott spent the last year campaigning against fellow Republicans who opposed a voucher plan he pushed during the last session that would give families public dollars to spend on private education. He has made clear it will be his top priority again. Abbott has also hinted investing in statewide water infrastructure will be a top issue, and Republican budget-writers in the legislature are pushing to add $6.5 billion to Abbott’s border security crackdown, Operation Lone Star. The address will air on 15 Nexstar television stations, including KIAH-TV in Houston." ($) “Texas lawmakers race against fundraising moratorium to fill campaign coffers, ” Dallas Morning News'Karen Brooks Harper andNolan D. McCaskill — “Few things focus the mind of a politician, and political donors, more than a fundraising deadline. For three decades, a blackout period around the Legislature’s regular session has barred Texas lawmakers from raising political money while they tackle the state’s business in the Capitol. The Texas Legislature meets every two years for 140 days. What lawmakers choose as priorities, and how they conduct their business, will affect the lives of Texans for years. Dec. 14 was the last day to raise campaign cash for the session that began last week, and the state’s 181 lawmakers responded to the deadline with gusto, raising a combined $13 million in two weeks — a number that jumps closer to $17 million when fundraising by Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, who presides over the Senate, is added. The dash for cash in the two weeks preceding the session moratorium awes even the most veteran of political insiders — particularly as the skyrocketing cost of running a campaign requires officials to raise ever higher piles of money. “Hell, it’s crazy,” longtime lobbyist Bill Miller, of Austin-based Hillco Partners, said of the biennial presession fundraising sprints. “There are multiple fundraisers every day, and they’re all over the place. There are so many fundraisers you can’t even count them.” One of the most visible examples was the parade of lawmakers and lobbyists into the Austin Club, an exclusive gathering spot near the Capitol where political fundraisers stacked up in one- and two-hour time slots — nearly 60 private events in the first two weeks of December. At the events, lawmakers wait in a designated room while lobbyists and other invited donors swing by with checks — sometimes getting a minute or two with the lawmaker, sometimes just dropping a check on a table at the door before moving on to the next one, according to several lawmakers and lobbyists who attended the events. The fundraising frenzy at the private club between Election Day and the session blackout period was just the tip of the iceberg. In-person and online fundraisers across the state had checks pouring into campaign coffers right up to midnight on the last day before the blackout." ($) | STATE GOVERNMENT “Abbott sends state troops to U.S.-Mexico border to work with Border Patrol, ” Texas Tribune'sAlejandro Serrano — “Gov. Greg Abbott on Monday said he's sending more than 400 soldiers from Houston and Fort Worth to the U.S.-Mexico border to collaborate with Border Patrol agents "to stop illegal immigrants from entering our country and to enforce immigration laws." Abbott said he will also send C-130s, an aircraft that can take off and land on rough terrain, and Chinook helicopters. The troops, part of a unit called the Texas Tactical Border Force, will join those already deployed to the border through the state's border security mission, Operation Lone Star, that Abbott started in 2021 in response to the Biden administration's immigration policies. Through Operation Lone Star, the state has deployed thousands of state National Guard troops to the border, though it is not clear how many are actively deployed. The Trump administration 1,500 active duty U.S. soldiers to the border. "Texas has a partner in the White House we can work with to secure the Texas-Mexico border," Abbott said in a statement. "I thank President Donald Trump for his decisive leadership on the southern border and look forward to working with him and his Administration to secure the border and make America safe again.” The move is the state’s latest effort to help the Trump administration with its immigration crackdown. Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham has offered the administration a to be used as a staging area for mass deportations — which an administration official ." | TRUMP ADMINISTRATION “Feds drop charges against Texas doctor accused of leaking transgender care data, ” Texas Tribune's Ayden Runnels — “Federal prosecutors dropped their charges against a Dallas surgeon accused of leaking the records of underage patients’ gender transition-related care in what some conservative activists are calling a win for anti-transgender activism. The request for dismissal, submitted by Jennifer Lowery , the acting U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, did not specify why the four counts of wrongful disclosure of individually identifiable health information against Dr. Eithan Haim were dropped. Haim, a self-described whistleblower, was charged after he provided conservative activist Christopher Rufo with the records of children receiving gender transition-related care at Texas Children’s Hospital in Houston, the largest pediatric hospital in the United States. Rufo published the material in a , however the records have since been removed from the piece. While transgender care for minors was legal in 2022 when the records were sourced, the hospital publicly had said it would end providing the care after Gov. Greg Abbott ordered the parents of children undergoing transition-related care child abuse. The Texas Supreme Court Abbott had no grounds to order the Department of Family and Protective Services to investigate the families. Haim never contested that he leaked the records, however he did maintain throughout the legal proceedings that no laws were broken because personally identifiable patient information was not disclosed. The case quickly became a lightning rod for anti-transgender activists and politicians who describe Haim as a whistleblower for exposing an alleged “secret transgender program.” Transgender care in Texas, especially for minors, has long been under fire by Republicans in the state. My Dear Friend, My name is Jeff Younger, and I’m the father to two wonderful boys. That’s my son James in the photo above.I’m writing to you because I’ve spent the last eight years fighting tooth and nail to keep school-appointed counselors, and out-of-control judges from transitioning my son James against my will and against all reason.You may have heard about my case from Charlie Kirk, Nick Freitas, or on Fox News.I am James’s father, but because I refused to accept that my 5 YEAR OLD boy should be surgically and chemically castrated......I’ve watched the school system, and the courts systematically strip me of all parental rights and privileges.Just recently, an LA Court ruled that my ex-wife is free to proceed with castrating my son James. That’s why I’m writing to you today. **[I need your help.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=4308f70311ca4572acbb5698fdebd159&_e=0X83dDVARKzFRf1ocKL5hQCUybWPFyGi_lD80wbqAk3xaoTS7xLJs3WjxW1wFULLZ3Su8UMAqvT_afI-LhTXWXsNCqWomswrSCZpv4CPVGkAt1x9BfKA1nVDh0tVrBOEO2UpeaJQzCl7a6m0JzBM1DZDFtc7IomO2neqzN86s1w5BXYwX6DqOoUuVLhYJNgr8uqm_u8_rBVh18GMASnIZY8JClOXCDe9UsbkkvWXMqDa7rCdbFe1SbFqo81Bjf4GNQcDJDIA0JkYtzcCecE9iVK8Kko9NC4FMqLeJyX1RbfsCVi2yYFvQhWokTOM-03Z3jhm_crv3T-4hYTrePx4Jod6OCILK5i_qne3pWf3o5dvBV7xJhFDyHCedMN4oCKA)** I’m up against radical trans-activist judges, the 6 BILLION dollar trans lobby, and coastal elites forcing their LGBTQ+ agenda down our throats. They’re trying to bury me in paperwork... They’re trying to bankrupt me in legal fees... They’re trying to break my spirit... I want to keep fighting, but I can’t do it alone. If you’re with me in the fight to **Save James** , **[would you consider making a generous $25 contribution to my Legal Defense Fund today?](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=4308f70311ca4572acbb5698fdebd159&_e=0X83dDVARKzFRf1ocKL5hQCUybWPFyGi_lD80wbqAk3xaoTS7xLJs3WjxW1wFULLZ3Su8UMAqvT_afI-LhTXWXsNCqWomswrSCZpv4CPVGkAt1x9BfKA1nVDh0tVrBOEO2UpeaJQzCl7a6m0JzBM1DZDFtc7IomO2neqzN86s1w5BXYwX6DqOoUuVLhYJNgr8uqm_u8_rBVh18GMASnIZY8JClOXCDe9UsbkkvWXMqBt4DAlxcKRDImTYFPaLvqXqJLY0GKT5alBSb8vZqrGCS1BQD4Zpmq36inCvBIA2qa95G6RnI0rzv9bj3HCukQQ89EjjaHtZuu_t2WYKS-Pg5NdyrwNDWuj8Kn-cKgaI20ACSl0LliRPZuxOU18geKm)** But I’m getting ahead of myself...Let me start at the beginning. When James was just two years old, my ex-wife began saying our boy James was actually a girl.I told her she was wrong, and I kept dropping my son off at school in boy’s clothes because **he is a boy**. (I can’t believe I have to say that.) I later found out that the school counselors were changing him into girl’s clothes once he got to school WITHOUT MY KNOWLEDGE to inflame this delusion.Then during the custody battle, the judge BANNED me from seeing my son.The court-mandated supervisor would ONLY let me see James if I put him in girl’s clothes. I have never affirmed the lie that my son is a girl, nor will I ever affirm it.So I was forced to stop visiting him.It broke my heart.**Do you see what we’re up against?** I can confirm that these trans-activist judges are presiding over kangaroo courts where common sense goes right out the window.They need to be stopped...They need to be held accountable...And **James** needs to be **saved** from their butchery.**[THAT’S why I need your help.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=4308f70311ca4572acbb5698fdebd159&_e=0X83dDVARKzFRf1ocKL5hQCUybWPFyGi_lD80wbqAk3xaoTS7xLJs3WjxW1wFULLZ3Su8UMAqvT_afI-LhTXWXsNCqWomswrSCZpv4CPVGkAt1x9BfKA1nVDh0tVrBOEO2UpeaJQzCl7a6m0JzBM1DZDFtc7IomO2neqzN86s1w5BXYwX6DqOoUuVLhYJNgr8uqm_u8_rBVh18GMASnIZY8JClOXCDe9UsbkkvWXMqDeS3of2DctNMqSDJWWGDE3KASqDeqjHkRsJSNhXBoTzDhY-VVd_UBqPILAudrjEh0AMB66rlxMW0iL8wLsGeip9lUzHW_Rls_K2l8Meeq-kOcSADA9f4AuQr478r9Le2R8JeQ7vkmrehlV69RcvGrn)** I am under a gag order currently to NEVER speak about transgender issues publicly.Obviously, I’m not abiding by that order because it’s blatantly unconstitutional.But that’s not even the point.If I were just some activist, maybe I would worry about the threat of jail time. But I’m not just some activist.I’m a Dad.I’m fighting to save my son.And I will never give up on **James**.I’ve been in court three times a week for the past eight years. At this point, I have more trial experience than most lawyers. I authored the bill in Texas, South Carolina, and Tennessee that outlawed sex change surgeries for minors.I then spent every dollar I had to make sure cowardly politicians passed those bills.But these Radicals are relentless and they don’t play fair. I got the law passed in my home state of Texas, but then my ex-wife just took James to California: a “trans sanctuary” state.And there was nothing I could do to stop it.And that’s the scary part:**If this can happen in Texas, it can happen anywhere.** Then in California, the radical judge railroaded me and gave my ex-wife free reign to proceed with the castration.I can’t even appeal the case because he sealed all the court records...I’ll have to sue the LA County Court to unseal the records just to BEGIN the appeal process...On top of that, the other side is trying to make ME pay THEIR legal fees...**Do you see what we’re up against?** But if Conservatives won’t put up a fight, how will we ever win? That’s where Patriots Legal Defense Fund (PLDF) comes in. They heard about my case and immediately offered to stand by my side. **[Will you stand with us?](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=4308f70311ca4572acbb5698fdebd159&_e=0X83dDVARKzFRf1ocKL5hQCUybWPFyGi_lD80wbqAk3xaoTS7xLJs3WjxW1wFULLZ3Su8UMAqvT_afI-LhTXWXsNCqWomswrSCZpv4CPVGkAt1x9BfKA1nVDh0tVrBOEO2UpeaJQzCl7a6m0JzBM1DZDFtc7IomO2neqzN86s1w5BXYwX6DqOoUuVLhYJNgr8uqm_u8_rBVh18GMASnIZY8JClOXCDe9UsbkkvWXMqDkDHo9veYJze_ggnJMCLi5Xaw_t3Y-Rh87AUt5EuyxJl8Fs5KlEYBEEqwEXqCO2ObLCzD5EWlYcHK60zMjc3Cn2ApiuhQ0akxqnPwG1ONkOtpwHAxXREbIS63vbL1nFpM4vYVBWrZ3AsPP5xw4OVIu)**

name: Katie Porter
subject: “How do we get Democrats to talk about the cost of groceries?”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Truth to Power PAC
body:
Democrats need to lean on and learn from folks who won in tough purple districts.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=39406%2E3422442%2EJIIWL8)
Derek, it’s Katie Porter!
During an event I recently hosted discussing Trump's first week in office, I was asked: “How do we get Democrats to talk about the cost of groceries?”
The answer: Run (and elect!) candidates who themselves experience the challenges that most working people in this country face. Too many families are being squeezed by the rising cost of big things—like healthcare, childcare, college, and housing, _and_ by the cost of everyday purchases, from blueberries to bacon.
When I was in Congress, it was *news* that I brought up the price of bacon ($9.99) in a Democratic caucus meeting. When I talked about how inflation has been hitting my family, it seemed like the first time the toll of high prices had sunk in for some of my colleagues.
Democrats should also lean on and learn from folks who won in purple districts, like Truth to Power endorsed Josh Riley, who won in NY-19—a tough swing seat.
This year, if you know of someone in your community who should run for something (especially if they have not been in elected office before) ask them if they would consider running! Whether it’s school board or Congress, every elected official makes a difference.
Truth to Power is committed to supporting candidates from all walks of life who will force Congress to prioritize policies that will lower costs for families.

Thank you so much,
Katie Porter
